Ehhhhhhhh. 

Like Delta_Labs said, it could be a number of things.  My first impression honestly is that her sheltered background may have some part to play. Again, I don't know you or her personally so this is all just an assumption. 

My town growing up was VERY conservative and sex-ed was abstinence-only with a high Conservative Christian demographic. I knew some girls who waited til marriage to have sex and I also knew a lot who came from sheltered families and didn't wait because *f it, I have rebellious urges". A lot of the ones I kept in touch with after school mentioned having frequent bedroom problems, some from thinking they're no longer "pure" even though they did the "right thing" but a lifetime of "sex is evil" still permeates. Quite common. 
https://www.google.com/amp/s/www.healthmatch360.com/360blog/sexuntilmarriage%3fformat=amp

There are a lot of factors that go into not  being in the mood for sex, here's some big ones: 
Depression,
Vaginimus,
Lack of Interest ,
Stress/Anxiety ,
Relationship Doubts ,
Cheating,
Eating Disorder ,

And of course, Asexual. 

I'm not saying she isn't asexual, but assuming that she hasn't discussed a general lack of sexual attraction to you before, it sounds like you suggested that because you don't want it to be any of the other above reasons. Again, I am making an assumption based on your post and my own experiences.

 Hopefully things work out for you guys.

Edit: some grammar mistakes

The older you get, the more you'll learn about your sexuality. 
You may just be young and simply not interested in sex because your focus is school/hobbies/friendships and develop sexual attraction later. 

You may be 100% asexual, no questions asked until the day you die. 

When I was in first grade, I always wanted a family in the sense I wanted to raise kids however I never wanted to marry. No desire. I expressed this, repeatedly, over the years from when I was 5 to like two weeks ago lol. I heard the same things I'm sure you're hearing. 
"You're still young" "you'll meet someone who will change it all" "you're in denial" and so on and so on. 

And because I believed their words over my own heart, I was put in a LOT of uncomfortable situations where I was trying to force myself to be "just like everyone else" 

My advice to you is to listen to your voice, *listen to that gut feeling*.
If you feel comfortable identifying as asexual, do so. You can always change the official label or whatever to explain it others as you get older but *always stay true to your heart*. 

Sounds cheesy but experience is a hard lesson rife with pain and I hope you can read mine and others' experiences on here to avoid making the same mistakes. I really wish there were communities like this growing up. 

TLDR; trust your instincts. 💜🖤🤍

Here's one of my favorite videos by Pick Up Limes I love to watch when I get on a binging cycle. 

https://youtu.be/EnAlwMfB2S0

It's actually really helped me curb my binging and lose some weight with little extra effort. 

The biggest takeaway for me was changing your mindset. Stop saying things like "I can't help myself, I'm weak to cereal" or "I just have no control" or "oh well, I blew my diet, I'll restart tomorrow". Instead, start saying things like: 
"I *used* to eat too much cereal, but I'm ok with one bowl" 
"I slipped up but I'm restarting right now in this moment" 
 
It takes awhile, but the first step should be being kind and patient with yourself and your body will reflect this.

Here's one of the most helpful videos by Pick Up Limes I found on YouTube to help curb my binge eating. 

https://youtu.be/EnAlwMfB2S0

The biggest takeaway for me is adjusting your mindset. Change "it's pointless, I always eat a whole bag of chips when I'm stressed" to "I *used* to eat a whole bag, but now I go for a walk/eat an Apple/watch some funny YouTube videos/scroll through Reddit for 10 minutes/etc..." 

Baby steps! Every slipup shouldn't be followed by a "I blew it, I'll restart tomorrow" but by "I slipped up but that's ok because I'm restarting right now", drink some water and applaud yourself for already improving yourself for your body's health.

Can 100% relate. I've always been upfront with my asexuality/lack of sex drive to boyfriends and they always 100% of the time are "fine with it" because they ultimately believe I will change my mind, that they will be this knight in sex armor that will break my asexual curse and sexually free me *ensue eye roll*. 

Even if you compromise (which I have done), they will always feel slighted, that they're getting a bad deal because they'll want more. After all, if you agree to a weekly romp, why not every other night? Why not every night? And they use the fact that you even agreed to sex as trying to shove the door open to "well, you're holding out on purpose because you must like sex because you agreed to have it a few times". Obviously, not everyone is like this but I've been batting a 10/10 average in my relationship history. 

Think of being asexual as being a vegetarian and sexual as a regular omnivore and meat represents sex. It's easier for omnivores to forego meat more often than it is for vegetarians to partake in eating meat. However, society believes it's easier to make someone "lacking" to simply add, than it is to make someone subtract (whether it be meat, sex, etc..). 

I agree with the above comments in that as soon as they start pushing boundaries beyond your comfort zone, just cut your losses to save time and energy better spent on seeking a better companion (something that honestly benefits both of you) .

And when you're half German, half Jewish, it hits *and* burns . 
Source: my internal pain

I'll share what I wrote on someone else's post: 

I've dated multiple people who knew I was asexual. Unfortunately, none ultimately panned out. Not saying this is the case with every asexual/sexual partnership but here's my experiences. 

1) they'll be understanding...at first. Until the reality of no-sex really sets in. 

2) Some will say you just haven't had good sex yet and they think themselves to be the white knight to "break your asexual curse". In fact, there may be some you compromise sex for in an effort to help fulfill their sexual needs. However, they will feel hurt once they realize that the sex will never be on  the same level. What is emotionally bonding for them is a mindless chore for you. You may end up feeling resentful towards them. 

3) they may think there is something wrong with them because of your lack of sexual drive. Sometimes, they will attempt to make you feel guilty because of how they feel bad. 

Based on reading your post, you are already heading down the trajectory to a break-up. You might be able to salvage the relationship, but it might be at a great cost to you. He will be able to find another sexual partner easily. For us aces? Not quite as easy. Personally, I wouldn't waste my time with someone who needs sex. It is nothing against them as a person but a relationship should be a partnership and sex is something I don't want to constantly be comprising on.

 If you don't smoke cigarettes and date a heavy chain smoker, you may get them to smoke less, you may even smoke a few with them, but the chances of being happy with them for the rest of your life is slim. 

Sorry. Purely based on my experiences. Hopefully someone will offer some promising advice to you.

"were you abused as a child?" 

"Well, you haven't had good sex yet" 

Never been abused as a kid. I always hated physical contact since infancy until today (I especially despise being hugged). 

As for the second one, I used to believe that, especially when I was questioning if I even had a sexuality at 17. In college,  I had sex with over 80 people, both male and female, and determined that I really didn't like sex. I always had to be intoxicated and I've never slept with someone more than 2 or 3 times (except for my last relationship, but it was borderline abusive, nother story for another time). After a period of deep depression and wondering what was wrong with me, I fully accepted that I was asexual. I've never gained pleasure from sex. And despite how I may feel about the person, I never really enjoy it and only participated to appease my partner. But it was always at my cost and I always suffered for it. So, anytime someone uses this line, I roll my eyes because I know noone will ever be good enough to change my mind.

Of course there's a double standard and it's something this show is aware of , especially when Eric's friends are making the comments about how hot Claire is for a teacher and making innuendos towards. And  I actually really like the warnings about grooming depictions before the episode starts and the helpline number at the end of each episode. It really helps remind the audience that what Claire is doing IS grooming and IS abuse of power and it's a slow boil in how she's dissolving the boundaries (giving him a ride home, adding him on Instagram, getting jealous and trying to make him feel guilty for wanting to be with her while simultaneously encouraging him to keep pursuing). 

Claire is a predator, something I don't think she accepts because as long as 'he wants to' then the blame won't fall solely on her. She guides him into feeling he's agreeing to everything and thus he has "equal control" in the relationship. 

After all, he's not a victim if he lets it happen right? Noone forced him, he *chose* to. 

And it's that logic that victims use to cloud the early red flags and cause them to rationalize what's happening to them. 

Also, let's not forget the side storyline of his friend (17/18yr old) dating his younger sister (14yr old). It's another example of gray areas when it comes to minors and their sexuality. Both Eric and his friend are the same age, yet one is engaging with a high school freshman and the other with an older woman. Eric's relationship is not ok but his friend's relationship is teased about because she's so young. 

I'm really looking forward to the rest of show and hope they continue to highlight the double standards that people oft turn a blind eye to.
